'''''Stapelia grandiflora''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the genus ''[[Stapelia]]'' of the family [[Apocynaceae]].<ref name=WCSP_512019/> It is commonly referred to as the [[carrion plant]], '''starfish flower''', '''giant toad plant,''' or '''starfish cactus''', although it is not related to cacti at all.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/stapelia-grandiflora-carrion-flower-giant-toad-plant-starfish-cactus/ |title=Stapelia grandiflora (Giant Toad Plant, Starfish Cactus) |date=2015-05-29 |work=World of Succulents |access-date=2018-11-12 |language=en-US}}</ref>  This "carrion plant" nickname can also refer to similar ''Stapelia'' species as well as members of related genera, including ''[[Stapelia gigantea]]'' and ''[[Orbea variegata]]''. ''Stapelia grandiflora'' sometimes also goes by the name of '''''Stapelia flavirostris'''''.<ref name=WCSP_511989/><ref name=":0" /> The plant is native to [[South Africa]], including the [[Northern Cape]], [[Eastern Cape]], and [[Free State (province)|Free State]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Asclepiadaceae/17384/Stapelia_grandiflora |title=Stapelia grandiflora |website=www.llifle.com |access-date=2018-11-12}}</ref>

== Description ==
This plant is a very variable species, with many hybrids.<ref name=":1" /> The stems can be either erect or ascending 9-10 (-30) cm long and up to 3 cm in diameter (usually less than 2 cm).<ref name=":1" /> The flowers are velvety and smaller in size than those of ''[[Stapelia gigantea]]'', they come in various shapes and colors.<ref name=":1" /> Flowers are intermittently produced in the late summer and fall seasons.<ref name=":1" />

The name "[[carrion plant]]" is due to the odor emitted by the flowers as a technique of attracting flies in areas where other pollinating insects are scarce.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/life/home-garden/2016/12/31/edison-ford-garden-fragrant-plants-southwest-florida-hughes/95755006/|title=Inventing Your Garden: Fragrant plants for Southwest Florida|work=The News-Press|access-date=2018-11-12|language=en}}</ref>
